memories.content: The instructions for one medication the user takes say to take it after the evening meal.
On a day with a morning appointment, the user miscalculated the fasting period and checked again at the reception desk.
For an afternoon visit, the user felt less rushed while preparing to travel than for a morning visit.
On a day there was no waiting chair, the user stood for 20 minutes and their back became uncomfortable.
On a day medication instructions were explained all at once and at length, the user failed to write down an important time.
On a day medication times were confirmed one line at a time, the user copied them directly into their schedule after returning home.
On a visit when their younger brother drove them, the user did not have to find a separate route home.
The user's younger brother prefers to receive a request for weekday-afternoon transportation two days beforehand rather than on the day itself.
The local agent cannot determine the current prescription or whether use continues from medication notes alone.
The waiting area at that clinic has too few chairs, so there may be periods when people must wait standing.
The user keeps two potted herbs beside a south-facing window.
During a week when the user watered every day based only on the soil surface, the leaves of one plant turned yellow.
During a week when the user checked below the soil surface with a finger before watering, the plant grew new leaves.
On a day the user left the window open for a long time, strong wind knocked over one pot.
The next day, the user moved the pot inward from the windowsill so the same wind would not knock it over.
The user put a plant-name label in a small pot received from their maternal aunt.
The user confused the care instructions for an unlabeled pot with those for another plant.
The user's maternal aunt considers understanding the sunlight at a pot's location more important than watering frequency when caring for it.
Before creating a plant-care reminder, check each plant's name and most recent watering date.
The soil in the user's potted herbs beside the south-facing window dries at different rates depending on the season and amount of sunlight.

analysis.overview: The frames cover independent domains: the reference records medication, clinic, appointment, and transportation experiences, while the compared frame records plant care, identification, placement, and reminders. No claims address the same operational decision, and no conflict or ambiguous cross-frame relationship is present.
